claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he:
- Studying A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent qualifications?
- In full-time non-advanced education (such as at school or college)?
- On an unpaid training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's doing his A-levels at the local college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying A-levels at college. That counts as approved education, which is good for eligibility.

Now I just need to check a few more things:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child) towards his upkeep, such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to make sure there's nothing that would affect eligibility:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that much and he's not getting any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **You live in the UK** – This is a basic requirement for eligibility.

✅ **Alex lives with you** – This means you're responsible for him.

✅ **Alex is in approved education** – Although he's 18, Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training. A-levels at college count as approved education.

✅ **Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week** – Working 24 hours or more while not in approved education would end eligibility.

✅ **Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right** – Receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit would stop eligibility.

✅ **No one else is claiming** – Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child.

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as he remains in approved education or training, up until his 20th birthday.

If you haven't already, you can make a claim through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
